proposal.description: A strike is counted on every change of hiccup_active, so both entering and leaving S_HICCUP add a strike
proposal.reason: Each hiccup now raises strike_level by two: one on entry and one when the cool-down ends and the supervisor goes back to S_SS. The cool-down level is wrong from the second hiccup on, and latch_assert trips after fewer hiccups than max_strikes allows.

proposal.description: strike_level is clamped at max_strikes-1, the deepest cool-down index, so the hiccup that trips the latch is not added to the count
proposal.reason: On the hiccup that asserts latch_assert, strike_level stays at max_strikes-1 instead of going to max_strikes. The final count read back for telemetry is one short every time the latch trips.

proposal.description: The latch is tested when the hiccup cool-down ends, on the post-increment count, instead of when the hiccup that reaches MAX_STRIKES begins
proposal.reason: On the hiccup that reaches max_strikes, latch_assert now rises only when hiccup_active falls at the end of the whole cool-down, not on the entry clock. Until then the supervisor sees no latch, and it moves from S_HICCUP to S_SS before shutting down.

proposal.description: The pre-increment -1 used by the latch test is copied into the clean-run clear, so strikes are forgiven one switching cycle before the clean run is complete
proposal.reason: strike_level goes back to zero one switching cycle earlier than clean_run_target cycles of S_RUN. If S_RUN is left exactly at target-1 cycles, the strikes are cleared although the original keeps them.

proposal.description: The clean-run counter saturates one cycle below clean_run_target, so it never reaches the value the strike clear waits for
proposal.reason: However long S_RUN stays fault-free, clean_counter stops at target-1, and the clear in the strike block (== clean_run_target) never fires. strike_level never returns to zero, so separate transients add up until latch_assert trips.

proposal.description: A switching-cycle boundary outranks the streak break, so a PWM fall on the clock S_RUN is left still counts as a clean cycle
proposal.reason: Say S_RUN is left (g_en dropped, say) on a clock with a PWM falling edge, and clean_counter is at target-1. The counter then reaches clean_run_target, and on the next clock strike_level is cleared although the clean run was cut short. The original clears the counter and keeps the strikes.

proposal.description: The PWM delay flop updates only in S_RUN, so on re-entry to S_RUN it compares against a stale PWM level from the previous run
proposal.reason: Suppose PWM was high when S_RUN was last left and is low on the first clock of the next S_RUN. pwm_fall then gives a false cycle boundary, so the clean run is counted one cycle long and strike_level is cleared one switching cycle early.
